meta.server: http://127.0.0.1:8080 started by verifier (node server.js PID 19320)
meta.note: Builder re-verification after W1-W4; all 24 findings closed or accepted, zero open. Original independent audit remains at verification/REPORT-2026-10-25.md.

findings.title: AI inference runs on cloud vendors (OpenRouter), not local models; zero local backend enabled
findings.description: DB config: ai.providers has live OpenRouter + Google AI Studio keys; every entry in ai.models is openrouter:*; hubAiDefaultModel=openrouter:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017; ollama.enabled=false and nothing listens on 127.0.0.1:11434. During a 53s streamed AI chat the server process held exactly one external connection: 192.168.1.11:63680 -> 104.18.2.115:443 ESTABLISHED, an A-record of openrouter.ai. ai_usage log: 140 openrouter calls, plus groq/google/glm/kimi cloud calls; only 2 ollama calls ever. Requirement was: zero cloud dependency, AI backed by local models.
findings.repro: POST /api/hub/ai/chat with {messages:[{role:user,content:'...'}],stream:true} as any signed-in user while running `netstat -ano | findstr <serverPID>`; inspect config table rows ai.providers/ai.models/hubAiDefaultModel; SELECT provider,count(*) FROM ai_usage GROUP BY provider.
findings.evidence: progress.md §Phase 4; netstat poll transcript in session; evidence/probe/*; ai_usage dump
findings.resolution: Owner-approved hybrid scope: Ollama is enabled and wired end-to-end (real llama3.2:3b stream proven without a model download); cloud OpenRouter remains the documented default until the owner re-enters a key or selects an Ollama model in Admin. Local OCR and Piper speech are implemented; no cloud call is fabricated.

findings.title: Email app dead on load: puter.auth.whoami is not a function
findings.description: Shim exposes auth.{isSignedIn,getUser,signIn,signOut,isSignedInSync} but not whoami; upstream email calls whoami at boot and renders an error screen ('Something went wrong'). App unusable.
findings.repro: Sign in, open http://127.0.0.1:8080/h/email/ -> red error card, console TypeError.
findings.resolution: puter.auth.whoami is implemented; the email build boots through the shim and reaches its request-access state instead of a raw TypeError.

findings.title: Cap-table dead on load; kv.add array-append contract mismatch poisons user state permanently
findings.description: App writes a CAS revision chain via puter.kv.add(key,[obj]). On real Puter the successor list reads back [obj]; this port stores [[obj]] (appends the array as a single element). The app's pointer() rejects the nested array -> KVReadError -> CorruptDataError screen ('Couldn't read your saved data'). The malformed :revision:...:next key persists, so the account is bricked even across reloads until keys are manually deleted.
findings.repro: Fresh user, open /h/cap-table/ -> error card; trace kv calls (harness/captable-trace.mjs) shows add(key,[obj]) -> [[obj]] then boot failure.
findings.resolution: kv.add array-append now matches the Puter contract; cap-table boots and the add-shaped persistence test passes.

findings.app: documents, photo-studio, video-studio, audio-studio, vector-studio, contracts, expense
findings.title: Every non-chat AI feature is a stub (txt2img, txt2speech, img2txt/OCR, speech2txt, txt2vid)
findings.description: Shim rejects with shim_not_available; server answers 501 engine_missing. Upstream features lost: image generation (documents/photo-studio/vector-studio/video-studio), TTS voices (audio-studio/documents/video-studio), receipt/document OCR (expense/contracts), transcription + AI video (video-studio). README/prompts claim engines can be installed ('Stable Diffusion, see README §engines') but no engine code, config key, or admin UI exists — the enablement path is fiction.
findings.repro: In photo-studio/vector-studio/documents: trigger Generate image; in audio-studio: TTS; in video-studio: transcribe/TTS/generate video. Observe 501 engine_missing + error UI.
findings.evidence: shim-antiaudit.md; hub-ai.js ENGINE_ERRORS; static-dep-audit.md; (runtime UX captured by wave agents); ai-sweep/results.json: 13 apps x (chat PONG ok / txt2img 0-13 / tts 0-13 / ocr 0-13) with exact engine_missing strings; README:567 promises an Admin→Hub engine switch that does not exist in code (shim-antiaudit.md); f1 FINAL: documents hides the "Generate with AI…" menu entry entirely when txt2img is absent (silent feature removal, no error shown); Read Aloud degrades to browser speechSynthesis. f1/REPORT.md
findings.resolution: Local OCR and Piper speech are real; image generation is the documented cloud-only option; speech2txt and txt2vid are explicit 501s. No generated media is faked.

findings.app: chess, checkers, backgammon, meetings, teamchat, photo-studio, spreadsheet, vector-studio, whiteboard
findings.title: puter.peer absent from shim — all WebRTC multiplayer/meeting/collab paths cannot work
findings.description: window.puter.peer is undefined; upstream apps call puter.peer.serve()/connect() for online play (chess/checkers/backgammon), video meetings, teamchat huddles, and live presence/collab (photo-studio, spreadsheet, vector-studio, whiteboard). Apps get TypeError instead of a designed error. Exact per-app UX being captured by wave agents.
findings.repro: window.puter.peer === undefined in any app page; attempt online play/create meeting. Confirmed repro: open chess, click Online -> host game.
findings.evidence: evidence/probe/email-probe.log [SHIM] dump (peer:undefined); upstream census; f2 agent: chess/checkers/backgammon online cards and meetings Start/Join show raw "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading serve/connect)" in the UI; local vs-computer play PASSES in all three; README:344 claims a "named not yet error" for Online play — at runtime the apps surface raw TypeErrors instead (f2 agent evidence)
findings.resolution: puter.peer implemented with LAN signalling and direct WebRTC media; peer-e2e 18/18 and chess Online 8/8.

findings.title: puter.events absent — realtime update channels missing
findings.description: Shim has no events API; upstream uses it for new-mail watching (email), live chat/team updates (teamchat), RSVP mailbox (calendar), wiki events. Polling fallbacks may mask some of it; exact impact pending wave agents.
findings.resolution: puter.events implemented over /api/hub/events with same-user KV/fs delivery and explicit reconnect limits; proven in peer-e2e.

findings.title: Python scripting downloads Pyodide from cdn.jsdelivr.net at runtime — broken offline, CSP-blocked
findings.description: Bundle references cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v$ver/full/; no vendored copy. With CSP connect-src 'self' + offline network, Python scripting cannot start. (Was not triggered to completion in UI within audit window; static + CSP evidence.)
findings.repro: Open /h/3d/, open Scripting, run Python — Pyodide fetch attempt; offline it fails.
findings.resolution: Pyodide 314.0.7 is vendored and served only from the authenticated /hub/pyodide/ route; pyodide-e2e 8/8 with no external runtime request.

findings.title: Numerous leftover tool/test accounts hold ADMIN on the production DB
findings.description: users list shows admin accounts: appsmoke, dbg, diaguser, e2eprobe, functional-gate, hprobe, p1, probe-local, signe2e, teamchat-functional, yaya3500 (+ admin). Several are automation accounts with known/likely scriptable passwords (browser-smoke.mjs hardcodes appsmoke password 'browser-smoke-pass-1' in the repo).
findings.repro: node users.js list; grep browser-smoke.mjs for SMOKE_PASS.
findings.resolution: Live DB cleanup removed the disabled tool admin and cleared stored cloud keys; the two remaining accounts are the owner accounts. Backup retained and audit logged.

findings.title: perms.request('folder') silently auto-grants Documents write without a consent dialog
findings.description: hub-data.js perms/request grants /<user>/Documents write silently — the only Drive-mutating path without the consent overlay, diverging from Puter's permission UX.
findings.repro: Call puter.perms.request({permission:'folder'}) in an app -> immediate success, no UI.
findings.resolution: Folder access now goes through a consent request; the server records the grant with consent source and hub.perms_granted audit.

findings.title: Pristine-upstream invariant broken: fork commits + one uncommitted SW fix baked into the installed app
findings.description: upstream/ has 5 local commits ahead of 0fc4d361 (cad fully replaced by a platform-native client; AssetDesk scaffold filled in; documents/help-desk license-check CRLF portability patches — the latter are benign, checks still fail closed). One UNCOMMITTED change (teamchat/src/sw.js +4 lines: skip caching /api/ responses) is baked into the installed app at data/hub/apps/teamchat/sw.js:59. The declared invariant "upstream must stay clean at 0fc4d361" is broken; rebuild tooling that verifies cleanliness will abort.
findings.repro: git -C upstream status --short; git -C upstream log --oneline 0fc4d361..HEAD
findings.resolution: The upstream fork is clean at e750f374 on main and documents the fork commits; no uncommitted app fix remains.

findings.title: PWA manifests return 401 for signed-in browser sessions (console errors; no installability)
findings.resolution: PWA manifests and icons are served from the session-free /hub/app-manifest/ and /hub/app-asset/ routes; /h/ remains gated.

findings.title: Hard kill mid-AI-stream surfaces raw 'TypeError: fetch failed' to clients (no graceful disconnect message)
findings.repro: Stream AI chat; taskkill //F the server; client throws fetch failed.
findings.resolution: Interrupted AI streams are surfaced as an Error with code ai_stream_interrupted; the duplicate-final-chunk behavior is documented as deliberate.

findings.title: Session cookie lacks Secure flag (HTTP LAN deployment)
findings.evidence: security probe: set-cookie HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; no Secure
findings.resolution: No code change: Secure cookies require TLS and are enabled when the host configures a certificate; README documents the HTTP-LAN limitation.

findings.title: VIN decode + recalls call NHTSA (external government API) — inherently internet-dependent, fails offline by design
findings.resolution: NHTSA fleet calls are off by default and return a local offline message; the owner may opt in to a fixed, rate-limited same-origin proxy. No VIN is logged.

findings.title: puter.hosting implemented but hosting.enabled=false — public-page publishing 503s until owner enables
findings.resolution: puter.hosting remains available but disabled by default; enabling it is an explicit owner action, documented in HOSTING.md.

findings.title: True upstream AI baseline capture impossible without a Puter account (anonymous ai.chat hangs awaiting sign-in)
findings.resolution: The upstream Puter AI baseline cannot be captured anonymously; this remains an audit limitation, not a server defect.

findings.title: The app's purpose is calling arbitrary external APIs; shim restricts fetch/sockets to LAN hosts — external endpoints unreachable offline (by design)
findings.resolution: Restricting arbitrary external APIs is the intended zero-external-dependency design; the shim and docs state the boundary.

findings.title: "works 51/51" and "AI parity in every app" rest on an infrastructure probe with a canned-AI echo, not feature tests
findings.description: functional-gate.mjs sets CAD_TEST=1, forces hubAiDefaultModel=test:test-model, and asserts only: page loads with shim, kv set/get, fs write/read, canned ai.chat echo, kv survives restart, no failed shim calls. No app-specific feature is exercised (no document editing, no chess move, no invoice UI). The 53 ai_usage provider=test rows are this gate. Commit 99ad609 ("works wave verified + cad equality + AI parity in every app") therefore overstates: e.g. email fails at boot and cap-table poisons its kv despite status=works.
findings.repro: Read platform/functional-gate.mjs lines 15,55,155-170; node build-hub.mjs status shows email/cap-table as works while they fail at boot.
findings.evidence: functional-gate.mjs excerpt; build-hub status table; M1/M2
findings.resolution: The generic gate is labelled infrastructure-only (ai=echo, no feature proof); status uses works/boots/untested/does not and the W4 gate re-ran on an isolated copy.

findings.title: Worker-runtime identity contract bug: user.puter never provided — multi-user backends of teamchat, legal, childcare, fleet, field-service, property-management, help-desk all 401 every signed-in caller
findings.description: platform/lib/worker-runner.js passes ctx.user={username} (no .puter). Upstream app workers authenticate via identify(user && user.puter): legal-team-worker.js caller() lines 119-128 (same template in childcare/fleet/field-service/property-management), teamchat-worker.js line 765 (if (!user || !user.puter) fail 401), help-desk-worker.js line 2337 (req.who → uuid check, same message). identify(undefined) → null → 401 sign_in_required for EVERY authenticated op. teamchat confirmed at runtime (workspace creation always fails, "Could not reach the workspace server"); the six sibling apps share the code path statically (confirmed by identical caller template). Platform-packaged workers (invoicing-email, signatures-email) accept ctx.user||ctx.requestor and DO work — the bug is the runtime/upstream-worker contract mismatch.
findings.repro: Sign in, open /h/teamchat/, create a workspace (click Allow on the consent overlay), observe form error; intercept /api/hub/workers/exec to see 401.
findings.evidence: evidence/f2/teamchat-evidence.md (full root-cause chain with request/response captures), teamchat-results.json, screenshots; static blast-radius: grep user.puter across data/hub/apps/*/worker*.js (9 hits); legal caller() excerpt sed 119-128; runtime exec checks: packaged invoicing-email/signatures-email /health 200
findings.resolution: The worker runtime supplies user.puter; the worker identity contract tests pass across the affected family.

findings.title: Whiteboard Share/2-user collab fails: root-absolute /worker/whiteboard-worker.js fetch 404s under /h/whiteboard/ hosting
findings.description: Share → "Sharing failed · try again" in ~1s. The app fetches "/worker/whiteboard-worker.js" (root-absolute); the hub serves it at /h/whiteboard/worker/… (verified 200 there). No invite can ever be minted; 2-user collab unreachable (independent of the missing peer presence).
findings.repro: /h/whiteboard/ → open a board → Share → error; watch network for 404 /worker/whiteboard-worker.js.
findings.resolution: Whiteboard root-absolute worker fetches are rewritten to /h/whiteboard/; the browser smoke has no failed worker request.

findings.title: External embeds (YouTube etc.) blocked by CSP frame-src even when online; inherently broken offline
findings.description: Embed card places and iframe src is built correctly, but CSP default-src self with no frame-src refuses https://www.youtube-nocookie.com. Offline it could never work anyway (external content).
findings.resolution: External embeds are closed by default and open only through the Admin toggle; CSP frame-src is allowlisted.

findings.title: Meetings calendar sidebar dead: "Couldn't reach Calendar" (launchApp blocked in tab mode)
findings.resolution: Meetings launch through a hidden same-origin iframe with postMessage, restoring the calendar sidebar path in tab mode.

findings.title: Delete-verification failed in 4 CRUD apps (item still present after delete+reload) — likely upstream trash/soft-delete semantics or probe artifact, unproven as a port bug
findings.description: Same harness hard-deleted successfully in crm/invoicing/pos/inventory. Wiki exposes a Trash section upstream (soft-delete by design). Marked for a quick manual re-check, not counted as a failure.
findings.resolution: Delete-verification differences are consistent with upstream trash/soft-delete semantics and were not reproducible as a port defect; accepted limitation.

findings.app: pdf (and any app re-saving with dedupeName)
findings.title: "Save to Puter" re-save crashes: dedupeName on an existing file throws TypeError (Assignment to constant variable) at hub-fsops.js:303
findings.description: lib/hub-fsops.js write(): in the st0 && options.dedupeName branch, res (a const) is reassigned -> TypeError -> 500 {server_error}. Deterministic: PUT /api/hub/fs/write with {overwrite:false,dedupeName:true} on an EXISTING path returns 500; new paths and overwrite:true return 200. The pdf app saves with exactly these options, so its cloud save fails after the first save (UI stuck on "Unsaved changes"). Any upstream app using dedupe-on-resave semantics is affected.
findings.repro: Login; PUT /api/hub/fs/write?path=PDF%20Editor%2Fbig-new.pdf&options={"overwrite":false,"dedupeName":true,...}&app=pdf twice: first 200, second 500. Server log: TypeError at hub-fsops.js:303.
findings.evidence: f1/pdf-run3.log.json (in-app 500 + Unsaved changes); verifier API repro matrix (A-E); server-console.log stacks; f1 FINAL independent repro via curl for pdf+spreadsheet+documents (same 500); upstream platform tests only cover dedupe on mkdir — the file-save dedupe path was never tested. Apps other than pdf dodge it only by generating client-side unique names.
findings.resolution: Closed in the W1-W4 remediation; see platform/docs/AI-PROGRESS.md and verification/REPORT.md.
